decision: MIGRATE generic schema-shape checks to AJV Draft 2020-12 metaschema validation; KEEP explicit ECMAScript subset projection and standalone runtime validators.
constraints: Offline Node build of repository-owned API-v1 contract must reject malformed keyword values before producing declarations or bundle.
Preserve canonical bundle and declaration bytes, closed vocabulary, local reference policy, tuple bound and runtime-only number/string bounds.
Validation error must remain fixed; no new runtime import, network reference loader, schema coercion or peer contract change.

alternatives.technology: ECMAScript with AJV validateSchema plus explicit subset guards
alternatives.assessment: Selected: AJV documents schema validation independently of instance compilation. Moves generic keyword-shape checks to its Draft 2020-12 metaschema while custom guards retain this narrower generator policy. Same Node process and JSON values avoid a second serialized tool boundary. Fourteen baseline failures and unchanged output tests exercise the migration.

Rejected for generic schema shape validation: observed string required lists, duplicate requirements and malformed bounds bypassed checks. Adding parallel implementations of standard keyword rules is less maintainable than a versioned metaschema. Keep only local subset rules.

Credible schema checking with explicit schema-error handling. For this standalone Node build it requires an extra interpreter plus JSON subprocess boundary while offering the same schema-shape layer and still requiring custom subset guards. No Python shared build service or other deployment requirement is present here.

Credible native schema validation and configurable reference resolution. This offline build requires no measured native throughput or memory guarantee; a cross-platform binary plus serialized Node boundary does not remove either the TS emitter or local subset policy. No native performance superiority claimed.

limits: Metaschema validity is not semantic satisfiability, authorization or hardware qualification. TypeScript declarations intentionally omit numeric/string constraints retained in the runtime bundle.
Input is repository-owned parsed JSON. Arbitrary objects, cyclic graphs, huge schemas and adversarial regex performance are not qualified by this build adapter.
This is a local incremental technology migration for schema-shape checking, not a language rewrite. Other language candidates were researched, not installed or benchmarked.
Runtime validators remain generated ahead of time; the generator may compile its local metaschema during the build. No remote schema fetch is configured.
